column4: In this chapter we will study the authority and power of Christ, which authorities and powers He has delegated to us (His church), and how to operate in the authority of the name of Jesus. We will also study angelic and demonic beings and examine their authority, power, and natures.

column4: Here are a few examples to help understand the difference between power and authority.

column4: Example 1: At work, an employee may have the talents and skills to conduct a sale of the company's assets (power). This power is lawful if they also have the associated permission (authority) from the company’s owners. Without this authority, selling the company's assets is theft.

column4: ## The Source of Jesus’ Authority
column5: ## The Source of Jesus' Authority

column4: Now that we have looked at precisely what authority is we need to know who the source of that authority is. Jesus’ authority is both divine and delegated. It originates from God the Father, is affirmed through His death and resurrection, and operates in perfect harmony with the Father’s will. Though absolute, His authority respects human free will, demonstrating God’s love rather than forceful control.
column5: Now that we have carefully examined what authority actually is, we need to know the source of that authority. Jesus’ authority is both divine and delegated. It proceeds from God the Father, is validated through His death and resurrection, and operates in perfect harmony with the Father’s will. Although it is absolute, His authority still respects human free will, revealing God’s love rather than coercive control.

column4: Jesus’ authority is rooted in His divine identity as the Son of God and is granted by the Father. The Father entrusted all authority to Christ, including judgment and rule over heaven and earth (Matthew 11:27). Jesus’ authority reflects the unity and love within the Trinity, where the Son carries out the Father’s plan perfectly (John 3:35).
column5: Jesus’ authority is rooted in His divine identity as the Son of God and is bestowed by the Father. The Father has entrusted all authority to Christ, which includes judgment and rule over heaven and earth (Matthew 11:27). Jesus’ authority reflects the internal unity and love of the Trinity, where the Son perfectly fulfills the Father’s plan (John 3:35).

column4: While Jesus had inherent authority as God’s Son, His victory over sin, death, and hell was fully established through His death and resurrection. Christ’s obedience in His sacrifice led to His exaltation (seated at the right hand of the Father), securing His authority over all creation. By conquering death, Christ gained absolute dominion over life and eternity.
column5: Although Jesus, as the Son of God, possessed inherent authority, His victory over sin, death, and hell was fully established through His death and resurrection. Christ’s obedience, displayed in His sacrifice, resulted in His exaltation (being seated at the right hand of the Father), and solidified His authority over all creation. By triumphing over death, Christ obtained absolute kingship over life and eternity.

column4: ## Laying on of Hands
column5: ## Laying on of Hands

column4: The laying on of hands is a significant biblical practice used throughout both the Old Testament and New Testament to symbolize blessing, commissioning, healing, and the impartation of spiritual authority or gifts. It is more than just a physical act-it represents a spiritual connection and transfer under the direction of God’s authority.
column5: Laying on of hands is an important biblical practice that has been used in both the Old Testament and the New Testament as a sign of blessing, commissioning, healing, and the impartation of spiritual authority or gifts. It is not merely a physical act—it represents spiritual connection and transfer under the direction of God's authority.

column4: In the Old Testament, the laying on of hands was often associated with blessing and dedication. For example, Jacob blessed his grandchildren, Ephraim, and Manasseh, by laying his hands on them (Genesis 48:14). Similarly, Moses laid hands on Joshua to commission him as his successor, imparting leadership authority and wisdom (Numbers 27:18-23, Deuteronomy 34:9). This act publicly signified God’s selection and empowerment for the task ahead.
column5: In the Old Testament, the laying on of hands is often associated with blessing and consecration. For example, Jacob laid his hands on his grandsons, Ephraim and Manasseh, and blessed them (Genesis 48:14). Likewise, Moses laid hands on Joshua to appoint him as his successor and to grant him leadership authority and wisdom (Numbers 27:18-23, Deuteronomy 34:9). This act publicly signified God's choice and the empowerment for the work ahead.

column4: In the New Testament, the laying on of hands is closely tied to the ministry of Jesus and the early church. Jesus regularly laid hands on the sick to heal them (Mark 6:5, Luke 4:40), demonstrating both compassion and authority over sickness and disease. The apostles continued this practice, using it to impart the Holy Spirit (Acts 8:17), spiritual gifts (1 Timothy 4:14, 2 Timothy 1:6), and blessings to believers. It also played a role in commissioning leaders and missionaries for ministry (Acts 13:3).

Jesus often laid hands on the sick and healed them (Mark 6:5, Luke 4:40), expressing both compassion and authority over sickness and disease. The apostles continued this practice, using it for the impartation of the Holy Spirit (Acts 8:171 Timothy 4:14, 2 Timothy 1:6), and for blessing believers. It also played a role in appointing leaders and missionaries for ministry (Acts 13:3).

column4: The laying on of hands symbolizes an act of faith and obedience to God’s Word. It is not a mechanical ritual, but a spiritual practice rooted in dependence on the Holy Spirit. For example, in Acts 6:6, the apostles laid hands on those selected to serve as deacons, committing them to God’s service and publicly acknowledging their calling. In Acts 19:6, Paul laid hands on believers, and they received the Holy Spirit, demonstrating its role in spiritual empowerment.

column4: ### Angels
column5: ### Angels

column4: Angels are a significant part of God’s creation, serving as His messengers and agents to carry out His divine purposes. The Bible reveals a spiritual realm inhabited by these beings, who are powerful, intelligent, and obedient to God’s commands. While angels are often unseen, their presence and actions impact human history and spiritual warfare. Understanding their roles, classifications, and activities provides us with deeper insight into God’s plan and the unseen realities that surround us.

The Bible reveals a spiritual realm inhabited by these beings, who are powerful, intelligent, and obedient to God’s commands. Though angels are often unseen, their presence and actions impact human history and spiritual warfare. Understanding their roles, kinds, and activities gives us deeper insight into God’s plan and the unseen realities that surround us.

column4: The term "angel" itself means "messenger," highlighting their primary function. Angels operate in obedience to God’s will, whether delivering messages, providing protection, executing judgment, or engaging in spiritual battles. They are not objects of worship but serve as examples of obedience and reverence, always pointing back to the glory of God. This chapter explores the nature, classifications, and roles of angels, shedding light on their significance in Scripture and in our lives today.

They are not to be worshiped but serve as examples of obedience and reverence, always pointing to the glory of God. This chapter examines the nature of angels, their kinds, and roles, in order to clarify their significance in Scripture and in our lives today.

column4: In the scriptures angels are seen as **messengers**, **servants**, and **warriors**. Angels frequently act as messengers, delivering important announcements, warnings, and encouragements. They reveal God’s plans and provide guidance in times of need (Luke 1:26-38; Matthew 2:13; Revelation 1:1). Angels are actively involved in protecting, strengthening, and delivering believers. They minister to God’s people in times of distress and provide supernatural aid (Psalm 91:11; Acts 12:7-11; Matthew 4:11). Angels engage in spiritual warfare, battling demonic forces to advance God’s kingdom and defend believers (Daniel 10:13; Revelation 12:7-9).

column5: #### The Nature of Angels

column4: Angels are created beings, brought into existence by God before the foundation of the world. While they are often referred to with masculine pronouns, Scripture makes it clear that angels are sexless and do not marry or reproduce. The man who was oppressed leapt on them, stripped them naked and beat them. Just as you should not impersonate a police officer, **don't impersonate someone with a relationship with Jesus, instead have a relationship with Jesus**!
column5: 1. **Only those who have a relationship with Jesus have authority over demons.** Acts 19:11-20 mentions the sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest. They tried to intervene in the life of a man who was under Satan’s oppression and torment, and the evil spirit refused to come out because they had no relationship with Jesus. The oppressed man leaped on them, stripped them naked, and beat them. Just as you should not impersonate a police officer, **do not impersonate someone who belongs to Jesus; rather, establish a relationship with Jesus yourself!**

column4: 2. **When an evil spirit leaves, it goes away for a time and will try to come back**. If it finds the place it had dwelled empty, it will come back worse. Matthew 12:43-45. When we minister to a person oppressed of the devil, that person needs to fill the void that evil spirit occupied in their lives. That means at a minimum establishing a personal relationship with Jesus and strengthening it by obedience to the Holy Spirit. Often an evil or unclean spirit has power to operate in someone’s life through the choices they made, based on their beliefs. Anyone delivered from the devil needs to replace that old belief system and be transformed by the renewal of their minds (Romans 12:1-2).
column5: 2. **When an evil spirit leaves, it goes away for a time and tries to come back.** If it finds its former dwelling empty, it returns in a worse state. Matthew 12:43-45. When we minister to someone under Satan’s oppression, that person must fill the void in their life that the evil spirit had occupied. At the very least, this means establishing a personal relationship with Jesus and strengthening it through obedience to the Holy Spirit. Often an evil or unclean spirit gains the power to operate in someone’s life through choices made on the basis of their beliefs. Anyone delivered from the devil must change that old belief system and be transformed by the renewing of their mind (Romans 12:1-2).

column4: We serve an awesome and mighty God, and we are ‘more than conquerors’ (Romans 8:37) over the defeated enemy. We have no need to fear our defeated enemy, for Jesus has given us His authority to crush his head! The devil’s time is short, and He will ultimately be judged along with every principality and power on the earth that rejects the dominion of Christ.
column5: We serve a great and mighty God, and we are ‘more than conquerors’ (Romans 8:37) over a defeated enemy. We have no need to fear our defeated enemy, because Jesus has given us His authority to crush his head! The devil’s time is short, and ultimately he will be brought to judgment along with every realm and power on earth that rejects the lordship of Christ.
